591:### F2 Summon on the fly
592-- Asked:       "A captain will move to the station position, emit the call when reaching the station arrival point,
593-               but then keep moving without stopping. In the basic case of a captain setting up on a single PR, it
594-               saves the stop and go nature of it (while still correlating the objects because the captain's call
595-               blip should match the arrival effect of the station)."
596-- Today:       Station jump-in (`facility.enter`, 2.8 s: tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600; E1 retired the
597-               beacon pulses) flies the summoner to a spot beside the station, holds it there through the arrival
598-               and a second named (`crewHoldMs`, 22 B9), then flies it back over 0.8 s (`stationJumpIn.ts`).
599-               Summons aren't director moments (not protected), so no lever shortens them, and they aren't in
600-               the crowd's `ARRIVING` set.
601-- Decided:     The summoner's path passes through the spot without stopping. As it passes, it gives **one call
602-               blip**, and the station jumps in at that instant, in the same hue and with the same ring shape, so the
603-               two read as one cause and effect (R8, R10). The hold and the fly-back go. The ship carries on to
604-               its next place: its next sortie if one is waiting (E4's P4), else its rest beside its work (13 §4).
605-               The summoner is named from the blip (E2: plates from the act) and its plate rides with the ship
606-               for `NOTE_MIN_MS`. The rule's phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival (a 15 §7 row). Under
607-               reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place.
608-- Acceptance:
609-  - A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors.
610-  - A unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place, and the station's act
611-    starts within 50 ms of the blip.
612-  - 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`. The schedule goldens are updated, and the packet names each change.
613-  - The ledger shows the saving per pod.
614-- Risk:        schedule (medium: every pod with a summon).
615-- Touches:     `theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts`, `engine/pace.ts` (`facility.enter` phases),
616-               `chart/fx/commands.ts` (`pursue` passing through), 13 §6, 05 §8 (M-row of the jump-in), 15 §7.
617-- Depends on:  F1
618-- State:       open
619-
620-### F3 Summon chains
621-- Asked:       "In the chained case ... he would basically move smoothly around the star system as stations appear in
622-               succession behind him (likely only fractions of a second between their activation) without [the]
623-               ship stopping ... Any action that summons a station within a short time period by the same captain
624-               (EG, same or adjacent workday OR within 30 seconds of the playback time) should just execute a
625-               smooth, chained maneuver like this."
626-- Today:       Each summon is its own `facility.enter`, and each station's first PR opening (`attachment.open`)
627-               waits for it. The nearest pattern is E7's Sector sweep (M-32): one carrier draft in place of many
628-               (`sweepCreations`, `PlannedManeuver.sweep`), revealing each piece in turn, with one note; and
629-               B-21/B-22's fuse, which joins raw beats into one without re-timing an event.
630-- Decided:     A **summon chain**: `facility.enter` drafts with one summoner, each link within `CHAIN_WINDOW_MS`
631-               (30 s, 15 §10) in x of the link before (a chain, so the window slides, unlike the volley's from its
632-               first), **or** on the same or the next working day (weekends skipped, the viewer's zone, as B-12).
633-               Two links or more. The links' raw beats fuse (B-21, amended: a chain's fuse may cross **one** day
634-               turn, F-Q1), under the same B-15 guard as `volleysOf`; a link the guard refuses starts a new chain, and nothing else
635-               breaks it (F-Q6). No event is re-timed (B-14) and a seek snaps to the fused beat's end state (INV-15); across a day turn, the day rule is F4's (Days). The first link
636-               carries one new rule, *Summons run* (`facility.run`, phases scaled by the count, like
637-               `sweepPhases`), in place of the links' own drafts. The ship flies one smooth path through each
638-               link's spot (F2), each station jumping in as it passes, `CHAIN_STEP_MS` apart at most (about
639-               300 ms, 15 §10); each station's tender launches with its station.
640-               **Visit order is proximity, not time** (decided 2026-11-06): every chain's path (F3's and F4's)
641-               runs one way round the system, all clockwise or all counter-clockwise, taking the next station
642-               along in that direction, never the next by its PR's time, so the ships move in an arc or spiral
643-               instead of dashing back and forth. The direction is the one that gives the shorter sweep from the
644-               captain's start, from the plan's places (pure in world terms, so seek and play agree; a new pure
645-               `chainOrder.ts` beside `sweepOrder.ts`). The stations are different pieces, so B-15 doesn't fix
646-               their order.
647-               Labels: the summoner is named; the stations come in at rest (T4) and claim no attention slots; one
648-               note names the count in the source's words (R9, R12; the wording is the planner's, e.g. *PRs into
649-               36 Repositories*). History keeps every event's row, and its *now* mark walks the visit order.
650-- Acceptance:
651-  - Unit tests: grouping is deterministic over the goldens; both window conditions chain, and F1's bounding cases

# 27 — v1.4: scope

**Status:** scoped 2026-10-29 with the user (`/sluice scope`), from the intake opened the same day when v1.3 closed.
Earlier plan: [archive/23-v1.3.md](archive/23-v1.3.md). Workflow: the sluice (`designDoc` in
`.claude/sluice/config.json`). Work files: `docs/progress/v1.4/`. v1.4 is the first tranche run under the sluice, so
its records stay apart from v1.3's. Fixture data only (INV-18).

## Goal

v1.4 finishes v1.3's leftovers and makes playback **a story more than a history**. Pulsar Pod (20 captains)
plays within a target time set from measured numbers, while Comet Pod (solo) keeps its full drama. Busy work
is told in fewer, larger moments that still name every cause (R13) and make every participant a hero.
Formations form up on screen and clear of their beams, with labels that don't collide. The chart rests
quieter: only what you point at, what you select and what playback emphasizes gets a full plate. v1.4 is
done when every item below is accepted, the human gates are signed, the frame budget (p95 ≤ 2 vsyncs) holds
on Pulsar under the profiles that bake the aura (`phone`, `tablet`; C3), with `desktop` and `laptop-battery`
reported soft with numbers at the final check (amended 2026-11-06), and 90-later holds only what was deferred
here.

## Rules

- The standing rules R1–R14: [13 §1](13-game-design.md#design-pillars). Most cited here: R1 (holo labels, four
  tiers), R8 (every motion means something), R9 (the drawn count is the true count), R10 (identity by more
  than one cue), R11 (an object arrives before its label), R12 (the ADO word first), R13 (playback explains
  itself), R14 (attention is budgeted).
- The invariants: [02 §1](02-domain-rules.md#1-invariants), especially INV-12 and INV-15 (playing to *x* and
  seeking to *x* draw the same thing), INV-14 (stable slots), INV-18 (fixture data only) and INV-19 (no
  individual scoring).
- Story time's B-15 (05 §8.3a): order within a piece is never broken.
- Values go to [15](15-reference.md) in the same change. Departures from 02 and 03 are amended there and
  called out.
- Project lenses for the sluice's agents: `.claude/sluice/project.md`.

## Order and blocks

| Block | Items | Why this order | Human gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | A1, A2, A3, A4 | Quick carried fixes. A3's vsync budget is the yardstick B1 is measured against | Final check |
| B | B1, B2, B3, B4 | The carried looks. B1 (resting plates) goes first: it changes every scene's labels, which D and E lay out against | Final check |
| C | C1, C2, C4, C3 | Measure before cutting (decided): the pacing ledger, then each candidate's estimated saving; C4 makes budgets and switches a device profile; C3 (split from B1) cuts Pulsar's frame cost as profile switches | **HG-C, mid-tranche:** the user sets a target per pod size and picks which E items get built, and how far |
| D | D1, D2, D3 | Formation layout before the director (decided): it fixes crowding today and de-risks E6's larger union formations | Final check |
| E | E1–E10 | The pacing build, limited to what HG-C picked. E1 and E2 settle what's shown and counted; E3 and E4 give the director its forms; E5 decides between them; E6–E9 build on it | Final check |
| F | F1–F5 | Chains (asked 2026-11-06, picked by the user, so not gated by HG-C): a captain's run of summons or merges plays as one smooth maneuver. Built on E6's volleys and fuse (B-21), E7's sweep pattern (M-32), E4a's transform from the gather and D's formation spots. F1's fixture first, so every later item has a case; F2 changes every summon, F3 chains them, F4 chains merges; F5 (added 2026-11-06) fixes Meteor's hit floor at the small window. After E9 and block E's audit (F-Q4); its own block audit | Final check (with D and E), with a live walk of F1's run |

**Final check:** the D, E and F stills and live walks (A and B were signed 2026-11-01), with a live walk of F1's run and Comet's feel; the Azure CLI live check (v1.3's E5, waived to here;
pass or fail only, INV-18); and the full suite.

**Sizing (a hint for the planner):** A1 is small (a clerk). A2–A4, B2–B4, C2 and D1 are medium. B1, C1, D2, D3
and E1–E9 are medium or large, by the planner's risk score: they touch the schedule, the interpreter or the
layout, which feed the goldens and the agreement between seek and play.

## Items

### A1 Station floor size in the gallery
- Asked:       Correct the comment and the note, and include the true floor size among the cell's sizes (23 F-Q4).
- Today:       `src/renderer/src/gallery/v1/stations.ts:70` (the FormSizes comment) and `:139` (the `-sizes` cell's
               note) say a station's floor is about 48 px long. It is `FLOOR_PX.facility` 57.6 as a half-length,
               so about 115 px long.
- Decided:     Correct both. The cell lists the true floor among its sizes, read from `FLOOR_PX`, not a literal.
- Acceptance:
  - `grep -n "48 px" src/renderer/src/gallery/v1/stations.ts` finds no claim about the floor.
  - The `-sizes` cell's note states the floor size computed from `FLOOR_PX.facility` (`gallery-v1` spec green).
- Risk:        none.
- Touches:     `src/renderer/src/gallery/v1/stations.ts`.
- Depends on:  none
- State:       accepted; docs/progress/v1.4/work/A1-A3/

### A2 `PieceState.outcomes` to the art kit
- Asked:       Move it out of the domain into the gallery's art kit, as a parameter only the art uses (23 F-Q1).
- Today:       `outcomes?: { m: number; r: number }` is on the view contract (`src/shared/contracts/view.ts:234`).
               The solar projection writes none (`src/shared/scene/project/solar.ts:169`: "always zero" since
               22 C9). It is read by the world art (`chart/art/worlds.ts`), the stage codec
               (`theme/starChart/stageCodec.ts`, `src/shared/engine/stageCode.ts`), `assets/seat.ts` and the gallery
               (`gallery/v1/worlds.ts`).
- Decided:     Remove `outcomes` from the shared view contract and the projection. The world art takes it as an
               optional parameter in its own options type, which only the gallery sets. The stage code keeps
               the field only if the gallery's stage strings need it. 03 is amended.
- Acceptance:
  - `grep -rn "outcomes" src/shared` finds nothing.
  - The gallery's world cells that showed outcomes still render them (`npm run e2e:spec -- gallery-v1`).
  - Typecheck, lint and unit tests are green. No golden changes, or the packet names them.
- Risk:        contracts (low).
- Touches:     `src/shared/contracts/view.ts`, `src/shared/scene/project/solar.ts`, `src/shared/engine/stageCode.ts`,
               `chart/art/worlds.ts`, `theme/starChart/stageCodec.ts`, `assets/seat.ts`, `gallery/v1/worlds.ts`, 03.
- Depends on:  none
- State:       accepted; docs/progress/v1.4/work/A2/ (amends 03: the `PieceState` block, the stage grammar, the seat row and `seatLook`)

### A3 Frame budget in vsyncs
- Asked:       State the budget as p95 ≤ 2 vsyncs of the display, not 25 ms, with the number in 09 §7 and the perf
               spec (23 F-Q3), and re-measure F10's frame time on Pulsar.
- Today:       `tests/e2e/perf.spec.ts:50`, `:90` and `:134` assert `< 25` ms. At 120 Hz the p95 flips between
               17, 25.x and 33 ms. The hidden harness window runs at about 60 fps (09 §7, lines 184–190).
- Decided:     The spec measures the display's vsync interval in its window (the median `requestAnimationFrame`
               delta at rest) and asserts p95 ≤ 2 × that interval, plus a small tolerance (a 15 §9 constant).
               09 §7 and 15 §9 state the rule, and the spec's titles say "2 vsyncs". Pulsar's numbers are measured
               again and recorded in 09 §7.
- Acceptance:
  - `perf.spec.ts` has no `25` literal; its assertions compare against 2 × the measured vsync interval.
  - 09 §7 and 15 §9 state "p95 ≤ 2 vsyncs", and `docTables.test.ts` passes.
  - Pulsar's numbers at rest, at 1×, at 4× and on seeks are recorded in 09 §7 with the date. (Playing may still
    miss the budget: B1 addresses that.)
- Risk:        none (a test and docs).
- Touches:     `tests/e2e/perf.spec.ts`, 09 §7, 15 §9.
- Depends on:  none
- State:       accepted; docs/progress/v1.4/work/A1-A3/

### A4 Station plate: no horizontal scroll
- Asked:       "The content in the station's label can overflow the area such that there is a horizontal
               scrollbar. We need to either increase the width of the label or shrink the width of the content.
               Either way, they need to match without horizontal overflow into a scroll bar. A vertical scrollbar
               is reasonable, but horizontal should not be necessary" (HG-B).
- Today:       The expanded plate's rows box sets `overflow-y: auto` (`src/renderer/src/chart/holo/holo.css:197`),
               which makes `overflow-x` compute to `auto`, so a row wider than the plate scrolls sideways. v1.3's PR
               stat line and run line (`chart/holo/holoRows.ts:150`) are the long rows.
- Decided:     The rows box sets `overflow-x: hidden`, and every row fits the plate's width: the stat line wraps
               at its `·` separators, and a long title or repository name ends in an ellipsis. The plate's width is
               unchanged.
- Acceptance:
  - WHEN any station plate in Halcyon's four pods or in Meridian is expanded, THE rows box's `scrollWidth` SHALL
    NOT exceed its `clientWidth` (a new e2e case in `demo.spec.ts`).

# Star Chart: notes for the sluice's agents

The sluice's planner, reviewer, auditor and fixer read this file. The hard rules in CLAUDE.md
(fixture data only, never a real PAT, the app never writes to ADO, `src/shared/` pure, Pixi v8 only) apply
on top of it. Grow it from evidence: each lens below is here because a review caught it in v1.3, or
because it escaped.

## Sources of truth
- **Values:** every constant with a row in `docs/15-reference.md` changes with its row, in the same edit.
  `tests/unit/docTables.test.ts` fails until they match.
- **Normative docs:** `docs/02-domain-rules.md` §1 (invariants, INV-*) and `docs/03-contracts.md`
  (shapes, IPC, launch variables). A departure means amending the doc in the same change, and saying so
  in the run record.
- **Standing rules R1–R14:** `docs/13-game-design.md` §1, and the active scope doc's Rules. The ones
  reviews cite most: R3 (the outside matches the inside), R4 (counts first, no reflow), R9 (the drawn
  count is the true count), R11 (an object arrives before its label), R12 (ADO words first, the metaphor
  beside them).
- **Art that shows a work state:** `docs/09-signal-ladder.md`. **Layout and sizing:**
  `docs/08-layout-solver.md`, which records what hasn't worked.

## Review lenses
- **The effect where it's meant:** check the change on the busy fixtures it's for (Halcyon's Pulsar and
  Quasar pods), not only on the default scene. In v1.3, a new setting passed every test and did nothing
  on the busy pods.
- **Shared Pixi resources:** `destroy(true)` and texture or geometry teardown can free resources the main
  chart shares. Check that the chart still renders after the new view closes. This one froze the chart.
- **ADO failure semantics** (`docs/04-ado-ingestion.md` §6): a 401 on a scope-gated call (threads,
  builds, boards) means a missing scope, not a dead token. One 5xx on one item never fails a sync. Reads
  go through the throttle, and are deferred where the stream defers.
- **Users' caches:** a migration must not wipe what it doesn't need to. Prefer clearing checkpoints, so
  history re-reads lazily, over clearing facts or team lists. Check the first launch after an upgrade.
- **The drawn count is the true count (R9):** no `+N` beside a free slot, no object without a reason it
  can state, and counts that match what's drawn.
- **Frame budget:** dense scenes (Pulsar, 20 captains) sit near the p95 budget. Any per-object filter or
  extra pass needs a before-and-after perf run (`tests/e2e/perf.spec.ts`).
- **Electron surfaces:** drag and drop, navigation and file dialogs. A drop anywhere off the chart must
  never navigate the window. Test-only seams work only in unpackaged builds.
- **Mode and state that outlive a session:** anything that switches mode (fixture or ADO, a tour) must
  survive Cmd-Q without leaving the user stuck.

## How to verify here
- **Tests for the files you touched:** `tests/README.md` maps code areas to e2e specs. Run them with
  `npm run e2e:spec -- <names>`, plus `npm run e2e:keystone` (~40 s). Never run the full suite per item.
- **Seeing a change:** `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` (examples in `tests/drive/steps/`) takes stills of
  the real app. Put stills meant for the human gate in the item's work folder, and name them in the block
  note.
- **Art:** `npm run gallery` shows every object at every stage, including reduced motion.
- **Goldens:** update only the golden your item meant to move; check its diff line by line.
- **Fixtures:** `fixtures/scenarios/` (invented names only); the Halcyon demo's coverage is guarded by
  `halcyonCoverage.test.ts`.
- **Shared `out/`:** e2e, drive, build and gallery all rebuild it, so one at a time (`with-lock.sh` when
  parallel).

## Vocabulary
The metaphor is in `docs/12-glossary.md`: galaxy, star, planet, captain, station, pod. Use the ADO name
first in anything a user reads (R12).

  `npm run e2e:spec -- <names>`, plus `npm run e2e:keystone` (~40 s). Never run the full suite per item.
- **Seeing a change:** `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` (examples in `tests/drive/steps/`) takes stills of
  the real app. Put stills meant for the human gate in the item's work folder, and name them in the block
  note.
- **Art:** `npm run gallery` shows every object at every stage, including reduced motion.
- **Goldens:** update only the golden your item meant to move; check its diff line by line.
- **Fixtures:** `fixtures/scenarios/` (invented names only); the Halcyon demo's coverage is guarded by
  `halcyonCoverage.test.ts`.
- **Shared `out/`:** e2e, drive, build and gallery all rebuild it, so one at a time (`with-lock.sh` when
  parallel).

## Vocabulary
The metaphor is in `docs/12-glossary.md`: galaxy, star, planet, captain, station, pod. Use the ADO name
first in anything a user reads (R12).

# Tests, and how to iterate quickly

**Status:** current as of 2026-10-27 (through v1.3 Block B). The e2e specs and goldens are named below, and the unit tests and
drive steps mostly are; the v1.2 tests and steps are listed in the v1 table's v1.2 rows.

Decided 2026-10-07: the full e2e suite takes minutes, so iteration runs a few of its pieces, and the
full suite runs once before handing back.

| Command | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` | Unit and golden (Vitest) | ~5 s |
| `npm run e2e:keystone` | One path per area, tagged `@keystone`, specs in parallel | ~40 s |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- <name…>` | Named specs, e.g. `npm run e2e:spec -- explore slice4` | per spec |
| `npm run e2e` | Everything: the specs in parallel, then the pixel and frame-time specs alone | ~3 min |
| `npm run bake:asteroids` | Re-bake `assets/atlas/asteroids.{png,json}` from the procedural asteroids through the gallery (23 C7); `asteroid-atlas.spec.ts` checks the atlas path renders (no missing frames) with its flag on | seconds |
| `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` | Launch the app, run steps, keep screenshots, state, console, and dev log | seconds |

**While iterating:** run the specs for what changed (below), plus `e2e:keystone` once things look
right. Run `npm run e2e` once before handing work back.

## Windows don't appear (decided 2026-10-09)

`npm run e2e` never shows its windows: they were opening centred, over whatever you were doing. A
hidden window still animates (`backgroundThrottling` is off in test mode) and Playwright still
composites it, so the pixel baselines and the review stills are unaffected — the whole suite passes
hidden.

- **To watch a run:** `STAR_CHART_TEST_SHOW=1 npm run e2e` (or any single spec). The window is pinned
  to the top-left of the primary display, and opens without taking focus.
- **`STAR_CHART_TEST_DPR=2`** launches with that devicePixelRatio (default 1), for checks that depend on it.
- **`npm run drive`** always shows its window: watching the app is the point of it.

## Taking ADO away (slice 5)

The fake ADO org can be switched off mid-run, from the main process, with no test-only surface in
production: `app.evaluate(() => globalThis.__starChartFakeTransport.offline = true)` (see
`tests/e2e/offline.spec.ts`). Three more affordances, all test-mode only:
- `STAR_CHART_FAKE_FAIL` (a regex on the URL) with `STAR_CHART_FAKE_FAIL_STATUS` (500 by default; 401
  for a dead token, 403/404 for a refusal that keeps the last known facts).
- `STAR_CHART_PROJECTS_TTL_MS=1`: the project list is normally remembered for 30 s, which would hide an
  offline start; this asks every time, as a real launch does.
- The `reboot()` and `forgetScopes()` test hooks start the app's data over, as a launch does.

**Source:** [06 §2](06-visual-brief.md#2-palette-and-type), [13 §1](13-game-design.md#design-pillars) ·
**Guard:** as listed · **Update when:** a text colour, plate or surface changes, or a target is
raised.

## 7. Maneuvers

In Solar, each data change plays as a maneuver: an engine rule (`src/shared/engine/pace.ts`) and the
theme's choreography for it (`src/renderer/src/theme/starChart/maneuvers/`). Lengths are at 1×.
These tables are the authority; 05 §8 and 13 §6 keep the rationale and the beat-by-beat detail.

<!-- table: maneuvers -->
| Rule id | Choreography | Trigger | Length ms | Tier | Protected | What you see | File |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `piece.appear` | Sensor contact | Story created, or Bug created as New (a sketch) · `appear` | 1600 | narrative | no | A Nav cyan contact ring tightens; the asteroid spirals in round its planet; two Nav cyan sweeps; its planet's sensor spark; a Ready grey settle ring | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/sensorContact.ts` |
| `threat.emerge` | Hyperspace emergence | Bug created past New, or a New Bug made Ready · `appear` (solid), or `climb` from sketch to Ready | 1550 | narrative | no | Space pinches in, Hostile red; a rift tears open with a Hostile red flare; the enemy ship slides out; it snaps shut; a Ready grey settle ring | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/emergence.ts` |
| `objective.underway` | Carve | Story made Active (also a reopen to Active) · `climb` → Underway | 2400 | narrative | no | The captain sorties beside the asteroid and cuts its facets with a Given blue cutting beam; a Progress blue flare as the carved look lands | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/carve.ts` |
| `objective.nearing` | Rig up | Story Resolved or Ready to Accept · `climb` → Nearing | 2400 | narrative | no | The captain's tractor; gantries build; a Nearing violet ring closes; stations the work goes to haul supplies (Haul); a Nearing violet flare with Victory gold sparks | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/rigUp.ts` |
| `objective.accomplish` | Landing | Story Closed · `climb` → Accomplished | 3400 | essential | yes | A Victory gold ring tightens; the captain's tractor; Victory gold stardust swirls round it as it turns to its platform form; it glides 1.2 s to its trophy slot (`CLOSE_SLIDE_MS`), a Victory gold streak following; the grand flare blossoms as it settles (22 C3) | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/landing.ts` |
| `threat.engage` | Engage | Bug Active or Resolved (also a reopen) · `climb` → Underway or Nearing | 2400 | narrative | no | A lock ring in the rung's colour; four Hero blue bolts; Danger red return fire breaks on the shield; stations add slow covering bolts | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/engage.ts` |
| `threat.accomplish` | Strike run | Bug Closed · `climb` → Accomplished | 4200 | essential | yes | Captain and reviewers make a pass: six Hero blue bolts, reviewers' Given blue energy; the enemy ship breaks up; a culminating explosion in Explosion orange as it turns to its caged hulk; it glides 1.2 s to orbit; the grand flare blossoms as it settles (22 C3) | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/strikeRun.ts` |
| `piece.off` | Warp out | Story or Bug Removed, Rejected or set aside · `climb` → Off | 1800 | narrative | no | Off grey rings; a enemy ship streaks away on a seeded heading; an asteroid fades to a drifting ghost | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/warpOut.ts` |
| `piece.reseat` | Reassign | Assignee changed, to or from Unassigned too · `reseat` | 2400 | narrative | no | The hand-off (22 C7): the piece holds while a Nav cyan route inks to its new slot; it flies the arc with a wake; a Nav cyan arrival ring. The new holder's captain flies to their planet to meet it, arriving as it lands, named *Takes it*; whoever made the change isn't kept busy. The frontier belt holds until it flies, then fades out as the last unassigned piece leaves it, or in as one comes to it (19 S2) | `theme/starChart/maneuvers/reassign.ts` |
| Engage | echo | `ring` in the rung's colour | The engagement has settled | — | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | gather | `pursue` sorties, a pass | Captain and reviewers go to the threat | The cast label | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | act | `bolt` six from the captain | The captain strikes the threat | — | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | act | `energy` from each reviewer | Reviewers back the captain | — | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | act | `charge`, `phaser` from each station and `act` breakup (Station fire, beamed) | Stations the fixes went to finish the threat | — | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | land | `act` victory, `flare` and `ring` in Explosion orange | The threat is destroyed | — | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | echo | `flare` grand | The bug is completed | — | 0 | keep |
| Strike run | echo | `ring` beside the grand flare | The bug is completed | `flare` grand | 0 | mutes first |
| Warp out | tell | `ring` Off grey | It is about to leave | — | 0 | keep |
| Warp out | act | `act` warp, `spark` streak and `ring` (a threat), or `act` ghost and `ring` (an asteroid) | It has been set aside | — | 0 | keep |
| Warp out | disperse | `ring` Off grey | It is gone | candidate: `ring` in the act | 0 | keep |
| Reassign | tell | `hold` | The piece waits for its turn to move | — | 0 | keep |
| Reassign | gather | `ink` route | Where it is going | — | 0 | keep |
| Reassign | gather | `pursue` the new holder's captain | Who takes it | The cast label | 0 | keep |
| Reassign | act | `pursue` the piece | It moves to its new holder | `ink` route | 0 | keep |
| Reassign | land | `ring` arrival | It has arrived | — | 0 | keep |

# F2 Summon on the fly — build record (round 1)

Built 2026-11-10 in one conversation, without the sluice's planner, builder or reviewer agents (asked for so), so there
is no packet, plan or review file and no ledger.jsonl row: this record stands in for the packet's list of changes and
decisions. Nobody was watching the run; the decisions below are taken from 27's Decisions where they cover them, else
by judgment, and recorded here. Fixture data only (INV-18).

## What changed

- **The rule** (`src/shared/engine/pace.ts`): `facility.enter`'s phases are the flight and the arrival,
  `gather 715, act 1200` (1915 ms; was tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600 = 2815). New `PaceRule.passes`:
  the crew flies through and on, holding no turn.
- **The sequencer** (`src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts`): a pass's draft isn't stretched for a crew hold
  (`durMs` = its span); its crew is free as it passes (`releaseOf` = the act's start); with P4 on, the same
  person's next flying turn may start so its gather begins at the pass (`passStartMs`); its attention hold lasts
  until its plate has folded (`heldMs`: the act's start + `PASS_RIDE_MS`). `passTimes` (open at the pass, whole
  `NOTE_MIN_MS`, folded: `PASS_RIDE_MS` = 520 + 1800 + 520), `passesPlay`, and `nearWaits` skips a pass (it never parks).
- **The mover** (`chart/fx/movers.ts`): `Sortie` gains a pass mode (`passS`): one Hermite path start → spot (at
  `outS`) → home, with no stop at the spot (bowed left by `PASS_BOW`, so an out-and-back is one loop); it keeps the
  ship until its plate's ride ends. A sortie that takes a pass's ship over carries on at its speed (`Carry`,
  `handoff()`; the runner's `move` hands `make` the mover it replaces). `crewOpen` follows the ride, and into the
  next sortie's flight.
- **The command** (`chart/fx/commands.ts`): `PursueArgs.passS` and `carry`. **The interpreter**: a pass names its
  summoner by `passTimes`, and marks the plate (`showCrew(…, pass)`); `labels.ts` sets `is-passing` on it.
- **The choreography** (`theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts`): gather is the pass (`holdS: 0`,
  `backS: 0.8`, `passS`); the act gives **one call blip**, a ring at the summoner (live, so under reduced motion its
  place) in the arrival ring's shape and hue at half the size (`BLIP_SCALE`), with the station's jump, flare and ring
  at the same instant. The tell ring, the fold ring and the land ring are gone (so the file marks no `repeats(`).
- **Docs:** 15 §7 (the row: 1915, what you see), 15 §8 (effect audit: tell, fold and land rows `cut`, the blip row
  added; `pursue`'s row), 15 §10 (`CREW_HOLD_MS`'s row: a pass holds no turn), 13 §6 (the jump-in row), 05 §8 (M-13,
  P-7). No 02 or 03 departure: `PlannedManeuver` and the IPC are unchanged.
- **Ledger** (`scripts/pacing-built.ts`): every item built before F2 runs both schedules with F2 undone (`undoF2`),
  so E1–E10's rows stay as measured; new `BuiltItem.passes` and `app` (every pod, Meteor too, in story time). New rows
  **F2** (undirected: the schedule's own saving) and **F2+** (every lever: what the app plays).

## The saving per pod (`npm run pacing -- --candidates`, story time)

| Pod | F2 before s | F2 now s | Saved s | F2+ before s | F2+ now s | Saved s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Comet | 45.8 | 45.0 | 0.8 | 45.8 | 45.0 | 0.8 |
| Nova | 206.8 | 205.9 | 0.9 | 171.0 | 170.1 | 0.9 |
| Quasar | 971.2 | 955.9 | 15.3 | 289.6 | 289.9 | -0.3 |
| Pulsar | 556.0 | 535.8 | 20.2 | 288.6 | 269.5 | 19.1 |
| Convoy Planning | 183.4 | 174.6 | 8.8 | 179.0 | 170.2 | 8.8 |
| Harbor | 189.8 | 184.7 | 5.1 | 179.8 | 174.7 | 5.1 |
| Meteor | 562.0 | 548.1 | 13.9 | 275.9 | 290.4 | -14.5 |

Undirected, every pod saves. With every lever, the director re-fits a pod over its target to the target, so Quasar and
Meteor spend the saving as story (fewer cuts) rather than time; both stay inside 300 s. Meteor saves less than its 37
summons suggest because each summoner still waits for their own tender's launch (`attachment.open` keeps its author
busy, not flying): chaining them is F3's.

## Golden and pinned-number changes (each named)

- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: `estimateMs` falls on Comet (53 065 → 50 145), Nova (188 375 → 185 455),
  Convoy Planning (187 265 → 178 505) and Harbor (199 565 → 190 805). Quasar 296 189 → 296 041, tempo 1.9 → 1.85,
  and it no longer pulls `light` as a lever (its 116 light forms stay, from the E5c light rules). Pulsar 294 434 →
  298 298: it now fits with short, montage and speed at tempo 2 (was 1.1), so its 72 light forms and the `light`
  lever go. Climaxes and the other form counts are unchanged.
- `tests/unit/sweep.test.ts`: Comet undirected without rising tempo, 61 845 → 60 945 ms (F2's 900 ms).
- `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-{ledger,candidates,built}.*` regenerated. The Summary's App s: Comet 45.8 → 45.0 (now
  10.5% under its 50.3 s yardstick, for the final check), Nova 171.0 → 170.1, Quasar 289.6 → 289.9, Pulsar 288.6 →
  269.5, Convoy Planning 179.0 → 170.2, Harbor 179.8 → 174.7, Meteor 275.9 → 290.4. The candidates are re-estimated
  against today's rules, as every item's run has done.

## Decisions taken here (no one to ask)

1. **Phases**: "the flight plus the arrival" read as gather + act; the tell (a ring before the flight) and the land
   (a repeat ring) go with the hold.
2. **The plate's ride**: whole for `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1.8 s) between an unfurl and a fold, so it is read as long as a
   note, and the turn-plate check in `solar-dense` (whole ≥ 1.4 s) holds for it too. The attention budget counts it.
3. **The blip**: the arrival ring's shape (0.7 → 1.6 radii), hue (At-rest blue `HERO_GLOW`), length and alpha, at half
   the station's size round the ship, so the two rings don't merge at the spot 1.9 radii out. It is a plain `ring`
   (not a repeat), so it mutes with the station's own ring and never without it.
4. **The pass's ship and the next sortie**: P4's park (`nearWaits`) never applies to a pass; the next sortie, when
   nothing else holds the summoner, sets off at the pass and carries the ship's speed. The sequencer test "no actor
   two at once" now treats a pass's crew work as ending at the pass (the station's arrival plays on without them).
5. **Ledger**: F2 is measured in story time on all seven pods (what the app plays), undirected and with every lever,
   since adaptive speed re-fits a target-bound pod (as E6/E6+ did).

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`: clean.
- `npm test`: 109 files, 1724 tests pass. New: `commands.test.ts` › *a summon on the fly (27 F2)* (no hold; the act
  within 50 ms of the blip, in fact 0; the blip and arrival ring alike; on the interpreter; under reduced motion no
  flight, the rings at the act); `maneuvers.test.ts` › *a summoner passes* (no crew hold, `passTimes`, no park, the
  next sortie's gather at the pass); `pacingBuilt.test.ts` › *F2* rows.
- e2e: `gallery-assets` (every maneuver demo, the jump-in cell among them, in full and reduced motion with no console
  errors), `solar`, `solar-play`, `solar-dense` (the turn-plate test now also sees passes, whole), `montage-names`,
  `camera-directs`: 54 passed (Meteor's 1024×640 VC-3 is F1's `test.fail`, F5). `npm run e2e:keystone`: 43 passed.
  Full `npm run e2e`: see the commit's run (below).

content.text:
I've built F2 and committed it as `cc978af` (`sluice(F2): Summon on the fly`) on `bench`; nothing is pushed. One problem is unresolved: in the full e2e run, `demo.spec.ts:439` (the A4 check that no expanded station plate scrolls sideways) failed. It failed again when run on its own, with a 30 s timeout. I haven't found out whether it's mine. The run's budget ran out before I could check it against the previous commit, and it may just need the spec's earlier steps to run first.

**What changed**
- **The rule:** the station jump-in (`facility.enter`) is now just the flight (715 ms) and the arrival (1200 ms), 1915 ms in all, down from 2815. The opening ring, the fold ring and the settle ring are gone. A new flag, `PaceRule.passes`, means the summoner doesn't hold a turn. The scheduler frees the captain the moment they pass the spot, so their next sortie can start from there.
- **The flight:** the ship takes one smooth path through the spot and on to its rest, with no stop. If its next sortie takes over mid-flight, that sortie starts at the ship's current speed.
- **The blip:** as the ship passes, it gives one call blip. It's the station's arrival ring (same shape and hue) at half size around the ship, and it fires in the same instant as the station's jump. Under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly, and both rings play at its place.
- **The name:** the captain's plate rides with the ship and stays fully open for `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1.8 s).

**Acceptance**
- **Gallery cell:** the `gallery-assets` spec runs every maneuver demo, the jump-in cell included, in full and reduced motion with no console errors. It passed.
- **Unit tests:** new tests check that the pursue has no hold or park, and that the station's act starts 0 ms after the blip (the limit is 50). Other new tests run the jump-in through the interpreter in both motion modes and check the scheduler's side.
- **Docs:** 15 §7, §8 and §10, 13 §6 and 05 §8 are updated, and `docTables.test.ts` passes.
- **Goldens:** only the director golden moved. The build record names every change, including Pulsar now fitting at tempo 2 with no light work, where before it played at 1.1 with 72 light forms.
- **Ledger:** savings per pod, in story time:

| Pod | Without the director (s) | With every director lever (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Comet | 0.8 | 0.8 |
| Nova | 0.9 | 0.9 |
| Quasar | 15.3 | −0.3 |
| Pulsar | 20.2 | 19.1 |
| Convoy Planning | 8.8 | 8.8 |
| Harbor | 5.1 | 5.1 |
| Meteor | 13.9 | −14.5 |

**Things to know**
- **The director spends the time on two pods.** With every lever on, Quasar gets 0.3 s longer and Meteor 14.5 s longer. The director fits each pod to its target, so with time to spare it cuts less. Both stay under 300 s.
- **Meteor saves less than its 37 summons suggest.** Each summoner still waits for their own PR's tender to launch. Chaining those is F3's job.
- **Comet now plays 45.0 s,** about 10.5% under its 50.3 s yardstick. That's for the final check to judge.
- **Old ledger rows are unchanged.** The E1–E10 rows are now measured with F2 undone, so they still match what was recorded.
- **Two tests changed.** Comet's pinned length in `sweep.test.ts` went from 61 845 to 60 945 ms. The "no actor does two things at once" test now treats a passing summoner as done once it passes the spot.

**Decisions I took** (none of 27's Decisions covered them, so they're recorded in `docs/progress/v1.4/work/F2/build-1.md`):
- I read "the flight plus the arrival" as the gather and act phases.
- The plate stays fully open for 1.8 s rather than counting its open and fold animations in the 1.8 s.
- The blip is half size so the two rings don't merge at the spot.
- I added an `is-passing` class on the summoner's plate. The `solar-dense` turn test uses it to tell a pass (plate moving with the ship) from a parked turn.

**Checks:** typecheck and lint are clean, and all 1724 unit tests pass. The mapped e2e specs passed 54 of 54, and keystone passed 43 of 43. Meteor's 1024×640 layout case is expected to fail (F1's known issue, F5). The full suite passed 213 and failed 2. The other failure, `solar-dense` "facing follows motion", passed when re-run alone; F1's record already lists it as flaky in parallel runs.

**Record:** the build record stands in for the packet, which was skipped since there were no subagents. I didn't add `ledger.jsonl` rows, because those log agent runs and none happened. F2's state line in 27 is now "accepted".
